{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVQjdzc8AAAABaqELWA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn3IVzhEQs6g", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn3IV", "number": 81, "title": "Schedule SH-2 interrupt entry and external vector acquisition", "body": "## Problem

Related to #17.

At `018eacb3aefa1318338511a5623e29b2ef2d44ff`, interrupt delivery has functional handlers and resumable memory accesses, but lacks a complete hardware-time entry sequence:

- `Machine::issue_cpu` captures an interrupt tuple at a scheduler boundary and immediately attempts exception entry (`src/lib.rs:689–717`).
- `Cpu::enter_exception` assigns eight states and issues stack writes followed by the vector-table read without scheduling the intervening internal phases (`src/cpu.rs:286–329`).
- The master external vector is calculated in `Bus::interrupt`; the transaction journal has no SH-2 external-vector acquisition operation (`src/bus.rs:428–454`, `src/bus/transactions.rs:57–69`).
- NMI pending state is cleared only when entry completes. SCU acknowledgement also occurs then, by querying the current winning source again (`src/lib.rs:746–755`, `src/bus.rs:458–468`).

The missing phases matter when another interrupt arrives while stack or vector accesses wait. In particular, a second NMI arriving after the hardware request-clear point can be erased by the current completion-time boolean clear. Existing tests establish useful handler, deferral and standby behavior, but do not establish this entry timeline.

This increment builds on the existing transaction journals, fetch scheduling and Issue #77 standby work. It addresses a shared synchronization boundary used by many subsystems.

## Expected outcome

Implement a resumable interrupt sequence for both SH-2s in the existing main-clock scheduler. Recognition, entry accesses, external-vector acquisition where applicable, acknowledgement and handler fetch must occur at documented phases while other hardware continues advancing.

Use the [Hitachi SH7604 Hardware Manual, Rev. 4.0](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/sh7604.pdf): §§5.2.3/5.3.8 and Figure 5.4 define external-vector acquisition using the accepted level, with chip selects inactive and programmable software waits inapplicable; §5.4/Figure 5.5 orders stacking, mask update, vector-number acquisition and vector-table access; §5.5/Table 5.8/Figure 5.7 defines response timing; §§5.6–5.7/Figures 5.8–5.10 define sampling and NMI request clearing. Distinguish request recognition from CPU acceptance and entry completion.

For the SCU endpoint, reconcile [ST-097-R5 §§2.2/3.5, Table 2.1](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-097-R5-072694.pdf) with [ST-210 item 7](https://antime.kapsi.fi/sega/files/ST-210-110194.pdf). Preserve the prohibition on IST writes. Document affirmative primary evidence for source selection and acknowledgement rather than assuming that the latest global winner identifies the accepted request.

Scope is the interrupt path and changes necessary to integrate it. Preserve existing architectural exception semantics, bus journals and independent CPU ownership. Other instruction microsequences, unestablished slave external-vector wiring and unrelated peripheral work remain outside this increment.

## Context and reproduction

The missing operation and late clear are directly visible in the code above; no new local test or complete suite was run during this planning pass.

`tests/intc.rs` checks vector modes, DMA handling and PAD latches. `src/bus/fetch_pipeline_tests.rs::sleep_irq_wake_discards_the_prefetched_successor_on_both_cpus` checks wake and cancellation. `src/bus/clock_tests.rs` checks clock-change standby and NMI return. Preserve these foundations and extend them with independent phase evidence.

The latest validation record, `docs/validation-issue-79.md`, reports 1,102 native tests and the complete 68-group browser aggregate passing. The supplied current-main CI observations remain in progress; they establish neither failure nor success and do not affect this task selection.

Technical agents may correct this AI-authored contract using exact primary references and rationale, updating the source Issue accordingly. Such corrections require no human confirmation and must retain meaningful independent validation and the fixed #17 goal.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] Record a primary-derived phase table before implementation: distinguish request detection, acceptance, internal states, stack accesses, vector acquisition, acknowledgement, handler fetch and request clearing. Reconcile the current code's table-number citation with the manual revision used. Identify any deterministic phase convention separately from specified behavior.
- [ ] Implement those phases as resumable scheduled work. Independent native traces assert literal clocks, access order, saved PC/SR and first handler fetch for NMI, an on-chip interrupt and IRL interrupts. Cover applicable autovector and master external-vector paths. Reproduce the applicable manual reference timeline, distinguishing ideal single-state memory from actual Saturn bus waits. Adding only a final latency constant must fail these assertions.
- [ ] Exercise external-vector acquisition through the transaction machinery. Tests distinguish it from ordinary memory reads, verify its applicable wait rules and ensure replay does not repeat acquisition or acknowledgement. Inject competing sources during stalled entry and check vector selection, retained unrelated pending requests and documented SCU acknowledgement behavior.
- [ ] Test NMI edges immediately before and after the documented request-clear phase while entry is stalled. Check which subsequent request survives and that entry completion cannot erase it. Preserve NMIE selection, DMAC NMIF behavior, SLEEP wake and Issue #77 standby/clock-change recovery.
- [ ] Cover both processors, SR masking, priority ties, delayed branches and protected successors, waited stack/vector accesses, representative CPU/DMA/refresh contention, and reset cancellation during entry. Compare traces across advancement chunks 1/3/17/10000 and passive inspection on/off. Retain completed memory effects without duplicating them on replay.
- [ ] Add a reproducible original MIT-licensed guest, or extend suitable original fixtures, to exercise timed interrupt handling and return, master SCU vector acquisition and slave/internal interrupt behavior. Execute identical guest bytes in native Machine and production browser Wasm tests. Compare guest-computed records and independently derived timing expectations; include changed timing/source operands, omitted-trigger controls and repeated cold boots. Hosts must not inject running guest results or bypass device execution.
- [ ] Demonstrate that at least one new phase oracle fails on inherited main for the intended missing behavior. Preserve existing tests and Star Collector, Prism Courier and Hardware Lab. Any changed timing expectation must have a documented primary-derived reason; do not replace independent expectations with emulator-generated traces.
- [ ] Update architecture, conformance and validation records with exact implementation/test/spec links, observed results and remaining deviations. Pass `cargo fmt --check`, `cargo build --locked`, `cargo test --locked`, native and Wasm warnings-denied Clippy, `sh scripts/check-fixtures.sh`, `sh scripts/build-web.sh`, CI-runner tests and the complete `npm run test:browser` aggregate without skipping required checks.

This is a partial #17 increment. Remaining CPU/peripheral, cache/bus/reset/DMA, SCU/DSP, video/audio/CD timing, BIOS/HLE/SMPC and integrated coverage requirements remain mandatory. Passing this task does not establish hardware completion or broad commercial compatibility; genuine BIOS and commercial-game compatibility remain unverified. Do not reopen old trackers or use closing keywords for #17.

## Optional validation

Additional deterministic interrupt-phase sweeps are useful. Personal firmware, commercial discs, physical hardware, human approval and live Pages inspection are not required.

## Required post-merge verification

None.
